card.name: Animal overdose toxicity descriptions
card.fires_on: Linking words and verbs right after an animal dose in overdose or acute toxicity text, just before the effects or signs are named (e.g. produced, caused, to, by, no).

modes.label: Verb after animal dose
modes.description: Verb or adjective following a dose given to rats, mice or dogs, leading into the effect.
modes.example: In rats, a single intraperitoneal dose of 12.5 mg/kg of chlorambucil produces<< typical>> nitrogen-mustard effects; these include

modes.label: Linking word before toxic signs
modes.description: Small word such as to, by, or an that introduces the sign or finding.
modes.example: Dogs showed emesis, salivation, and tremors at a C max 41 times the human therapeutic C max , progressing<< to>> sedation and convulsions at higher

modes.label: No effect wording
modes.description: The word no before adverse effects after a high animal dose.
modes.example: In acute rodent toxicity studies, a single oral 5600 mg/kg dose produced<< no>> adverse effects.

card.writes: It seems to push the next words toward clinical signs and symptoms.
card.plain: It fires in animal overdose passages at the word just before the toxic effects are described.
